svg.title: Why a behaviour test could not catch this, and what does
svg.desc: A behaviour test writes rows through a mock, which applies column defaults correctly, so the null never appears and the test passes. It also sorts an in-memory array, where null ordering differs from the database. The bug is invisible to it. A source-shape test instead reads the repository's own source and asserts three structural properties: that no descending sort over the message table omits the nulls-last modifier, that no multi-row insert omits the timestamp column, and that the specific query the agent reads still carries the guard, asserted by name so a refactor cannot quietly drop it.
svg.text: Writes through a mock, sorts in memory
The mock applies the column default, so the null never appears.
The in-memory sort orders nulls differently from the database.
Passes. Has proved nothing about either default.
Reads the repository's own source, asserts structure
1 · No descending sort over the message table omits the nulls-last modifier
2 · No multi-row insert omits the timestamp column
3 · The exact query the agent reads still carries the guard,
asserted by name, so a rename cannot silently drop it
Fails the moment someone reintroduces either shape.
When a bug lives in the gap between two libraries' defaults,
the thing worth pinning is the shape of the code, not its behaviour.
